note: Sri Lanka's largest private banks are Commercial Bank, Hatton National Bank, Sampath and Seylan (with the state Bank of Ceylon and People's Bank). Commercial Bank's and HNB's sites didn't answer this research (no connection, 2026-10-30) and Sampath's card page shows a captcha, which this research doesn't pass; so Seylan Bank, this file's bank since 2026-10-29, is written alone. Seylan's Mastercard Freedom page (read again 2026-10-30): 28.00% a year from 1 July 2026; no fee but a maintenance charge of 1,500 rupees in a billing cycle with less than 10,000 rupees spent (kept, as written since 2026-10-29, as a monthly fee waived by that spending); up to 51 days free of interest; on spending abroad an added amount of at least 4.50%, written as 4.50%. Seylan's service charges page (read 2026-10-30), each credit card's table: 28.00% a year from 1 July 2026; the annual fee and the joining fee (written as the issue fee): Visa Platinum 3,500 and 2,750 rupees, Visa Gold 2,500 and 1,250, World Mastercard and Visa Signature 6,000 and 2,750 (marked with an asterisk whose note wasn't found), Visa Infinite free; up to 51 days free of interest on purchases when paid in full; a late payment 2,000 rupees; over the limit 1,950 rupees (from 9 March 2026); a cash advance 700 rupees or 4.00%, whichever is higher; a cheque returned 'refer to drawer' 2,000 rupees (Platinum and Gold; other reasons 1,000, not written); spending abroad at least 4.50% added (the 3.5% on overseas spending billed in rupees isn't written). The SMS alert fee of 500 a year, the paper-statement fee and the corporate and cash-backed cards aren't written. No minimum payment is stated.
